concepts.def: Systematically observing and measuring performance, using data such as success rates to identify strengths and weaknesses.
Recording events during performance (e.g. passes, shots) to produce objective data for analysis.
Targets that are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic and Time-bound, used to focus a development programme.
Frequency, Intensity, Time and Type, applied so that training is appropriate and produces improvement.
Gradually increasing the training demand so the body keeps adapting and performance continues to improve.
Dividing a training year into phases (macro-, meso-, microcycles) to peak at the right time and aid recovery.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Performance Analysis and Performance Development Programme — a core area of A-Level PE.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Performance Analysis and Performance Development Programme brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Performance Analysis and Performance Development Programme.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does the 'S' in SMART goals stand for?
options: Specific
Strong
Simple
Slow
Objective data about performance, e.g. number of successful passes
A random opinion only
A training diet
A first-aid plan
Gradually increasing training demands to drive adaptation

mcqs.q: In the FITT principle, what does 'T' (Type) refer to?
options: The kind of training used (e.g. interval, continuous)
The time of day only
The team's name
The temperature

Strong
